recommendation_basis: Frozen validation comparison; not selected using test metrics.
latency_protocol: Sequential single-query warm-corpus retrieval, no network, fixed CPU threads. Learned latency is measured RRF retrieval plus reranking; model/index build excluded. No encoder-result cache; RRF/dense queries include encoding. Methods run in a fixed order, so timing is descriptive, not a controlled performance comparison.

ranker_training.candidate_ablation_note: No-dense feature ablation uses identical hybrid candidates; this isolates feature effects, not dense retrieval effects.

split.group_definition: connected components of shared positive documents or equal lowercase punctuation-free claims with digits normalized

ranker_training.selection_metric: validation ndcg@10; stable first-grid-item tie break
ranker_training.positive_injection_policy: Only supervised training matrices contain missing gold positives. Validation/test ranked pools are untouched. Final refit uses all official train queries.
ranker_training.unjudged_policy: Unjudged training candidates are assigned label zero; sparse judgments can create false negatives.

retrieval_metadata.rrf_zero_bm25_policy: exclude lexical vote for nonmatching documents

split_audit.note: Official test partition preserved. Shared corpus documents are allowed in retrieval; normalized-claim overlap is reported as an evaluation limitation when nonzero.

limitations: SciFact is a small, English scientific-evidence retrieval benchmark; results do not establish performance on private company documents or Chinese queries.
The dense encoder is pretrained and frozen. This experiment trains LambdaMART only; it does not fine-tune an LLM or train a cross-encoder.
Public encoder pretraining data can overlap public benchmarks; no claim of contamination-free neural evaluation is made.
Unjudged documents are treated as nonrelevant; evidence judgments can be incomplete.
The official corpus is available during indexing/training; this is a transductive document retrieval benchmark.
Bootstrap intervals resample queries, not related claim groups, and do not adjust for multiple comparisons.
No-dense ablation removes dense and RRF features but keeps the same hybrid candidate pool; it does not ablate dense candidate generation.
